item.title: Card #202: Offenbach am Main, Hesse, Germany — Blick in die Bieberer Straße (c. mid-1950s (20pf Heuss Bundespost stamps, issued 1954–1960; postmark date not fully legible))
item.description: Inge writes home to St. Louis from Offenbach am Main, back in Germany to care for her ailing mother and hoping to bring her to the States — a quieter, harder note than most in the archive.

item.title: Card #201: Government Camp, Oregon — Timberline Lodge, Mount Hood (January 3, 1981)
item.description: Jan writes home from a snowy, high-altitude visit to Timberline Lodge in January 1981, promising Stella in New Bedford, Mass. a view worth the trip.

item.title: Card #200: South Fork, Colorado — Northwest Coast Masks, Museum of Mankind (August 9, 1977)
item.description: Geo. & Alice settle back into their South Fork, Colorado cabin for the summer of 1977 — feeders full of birds, an elk-and-deer barbeque on the calendar — sent on a British Museum mask souvenir card.

item.title: Card #199: Copenhagen, Denmark — Fredensborg Castle (August 13, 1952)
item.description: A quick hello from an international convention in Copenhagen, 1952 — sent to Edith Stoughton in Napoleon, Ohio, on a postcard of the king's summer castle at Fredensborg.

item.title: Card #198: Colorado (San Luis Valley) — "Peace on Earth" Christmas Postcard (December 18, 1915)
item.description: Leta writes her brother Herbert in San Acacio, Colorado just before Christmas 1915, checking on his cold and passing along family news before heading off herself for the holiday.

item.title: Card #197: St. Louis, Missouri — Bluff Scene along Mississippi River (May 16, 1911)
item.description: A cousin's gentle nudge from St. Louis to Kansas City in 1911 — "haven't heard from you for so long" — sent on a scenic Mississippi River bluff card.

media:thumbnail.url: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jeremy5ive/foundandsent/main/images/1911 - Bluff Scene, Mississippi River, MO - front.jpeg

item.description: Minnie writes to Ellen in New York in 1909, breaking the news that Mary has left the household — but still angling for that promised visit to South Orange.

media:thumbnail.url: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jeremy5ive/foundandsent/main/images/1909 - Askeaton Abbey Monastery - Limerick, Ireland - front.jpeg

item.title: Card #195: Trappenkamp, Schleswig-Holstein, Germany (c. 1950s–1960s (undated — see notes))
item.description: A birthday greeting from Trappenkamp, Germany — a town built from a WWII naval depot turned refugee settlement — to cousin Albert Hueske at the same Houston address as another card already in the archive.

item.title: Card #194: Hector Falls, New York (near Watkins Glen) (c. 1968–1971 (undated — see notes))
item.description: A postcard from Hector Falls near Watkins Glen, NY — ‘Ma’ Hadden writes to a friend in Sanford, Maine about a Finger Lakes trip with a Niagara Falls stop still to come.

item.title: Card #193: Fort Worth, Texas (c. 1980s (undated — see notes))
item.description: An undated Fort Worth skyline postcard, never mailed — Fred, Linda & Christy write to Robert Bowman in Shelbyville, Illinois about a graduation trip.

item.title: Card #191: Allenstein, East Prussia (now Olsztyn, Poland) — Castle (October 13, 1917)
item.description: A WWI Feldpost card from Allenstein Castle (now Olsztyn, Poland) — once Copernicus's home base — signed by a group of soldiers sending greetings to a wife back in Berlin, October 1917.

item.title: Card #190: Hoover Dam, Nevada/Arizona border (February 14, 1966)
item.description: A 1966 Valentine's Day postcard from Las Vegas — Rudy sends quick greetings from Hoover Dam to the whole ‘Court House Gang’ back in Warsaw, Missouri.

item.description: A 1948 postcard of Nashville's illuminated Parthenon reflected in Lake Watauga, with a mother writing to her son's church in Lexington, Kentucky about a stop in Cottontown, TN.

item.description: A Dallas postcard mailed just eight days after JFK's assassination — ‘we are seeing the place that saddened the nation,’ a family writes home from the Meadows Building.

item.title: Card #187: Rio de Janeiro, Brazil — Candelária Church (July 31, 1963)

item.title: Card #183: Reno, Nevada — University of Nevada (June 1949 (Thursday))
item.description: A 1949 University of Nevada, Reno postcard — Bill marks their lodging with an X on the front and jokes about losing dimes to a payphone.

item.title: Card #182: Pana, Illinois — Pana Township High School (July 20, 1921)
item.description: A 1921 postcard of Pana Township High School in Illinois, with Bert writing to Mrs. Luther Davidson in nearby Findlay about a trip to the Shelbyville carnival.

item.description: A German family postcard from Bochum's Schauspielhaus, airmailed to Elisabeth Pfanneberg in Lexington, Massachusetts — the German cursive resists full translation, but it's clearly a warm, multi-signature family letter. Ballparked to the mid-to-late 1950s.

item.title: Card #180: Michigan — Autumn Woodland Road (c. 1955 (estimated from printer's code — card was never mailed))
item.description: An unmailed “Fall Color Tour” postcard from Michigan, written in Portuguese and never sent — the message admits the photo doesn't quite do the scene justice, but it gives you an idea. Ballparked to the mid-1950s from a printer's code.

item.title: Card #179: Great Smoky Mountains National Park — Loop-Over Underpass (April 20, 1961)
item.description: Bernice writes home mid-road-trip through the Smokies in April 1961, raving about the scenery from a stop near Chattanooga — sent on a card featuring U.S. 441's famous spiraling Loop-Over Underpass.

item.title: Card #178: Myrtle Beach, South Carolina — Ocean Plaza Pier (June 14, 1960)

item.title: Card #177: South Texas — Palm-Lined Boulevard (June 25, 1957)
item.description: Helen writes “Dear Art” from Harlingen, Texas in June 1957, mid-road-trip toward Brownsville with a storm rolling in — sent home on a palm-lined South Texas postcard by McAllen photographer Don Bartels.

item.title: Card #176: Tallahassee, Florida — Lake Bradford, “The Disappearing Lake” (June 10, 1935)
item.description: A scout writes to “Dear Scoutmaster” Rev. Wm. Wallace in June 1935, apologizing for not living up to expectations and promising to make it right — mailed from beside Tallahassee’s Lake Bradford, known locally as “the Disappearing Lake.”

item.title: Card #175: Braymer, Missouri — Farm Scene, Milking Time (June 26, 1923)
item.description: A daughter’s quick note home from Braymer, Missouri in June 1923, on a mass-produced “farm scene” postcard overprinted for the local market — hoping folks are well and promising a letter before long.

item.title: Card #167: Bonn, Germany — Bonn am Rhein (July 7, 2003)
item.description: From: Betti & Wilhelm, Bonn, Germany | To: Familie Albert Huerske, Houston, Texas, USA | Written July 7, 2003. Hans Verlag / Hadres Verlag, Hamburg. Stunning black and white multi-view of Bonn am Rhein — Rhine, Bonn Minster, Bundeshaus, Beethovenhaus, Villa Hammerschmidt. Message: “We were with the Pomeranian regional association in Bonn and thought of you. We saw the Federal Parliament assembly hall where Kennedy once was. Warm greetings, Betti & Wilhelm.”

item.title: Card #166: Nashville, Tennessee — Music City U.S.A. (1987)
item.description: From: Bob & Theresa, Nashville, TN | To: Mr. & Mrs. L. McClelland, 9 Robs Lane, Sharon, Mass. 02067 | Sinclair Lewis 14¢ stamp, postmarked Nashville, 1987. Southern Post Card Co. Aerial photo of Music City U.S.A. Message: “Flight was smooth, less than two hours. Did night tours on Sat, all day tours on Sun. Tomorrow booked for dinner cruise on the Belle Carol. Hope to get tickets for Grand Ole Opry.”

item.title: Card #165: Ruskin, Florida — Quality Inn Bahia Beach (c. 1978)
item.description: From: Alice & Arnold, Ruskin, FL | To: Mrs. Joseph Chisholm, 12 Durant Ave., Dedham, Mass. | USA 9¢ stamp, postmarked Tampa, FL, c. 1978. International Graphics. Color photo of Quality Inn Bahia Beach with pool and marina. Message: “Dear Helen: Staying here for a few days. Lovely place for a rest. Today it’s 80° with the wind off the ocean. Love, Alice & Arnold.”

item.title: Card #164: Greenwood Lake, New Jersey (August 1, 1941)
item.description: From: John & Irene | To: Mr. & Mrs. L. McClelland, 29 Jackson Ave., Jersey City, NJ | “For Defense” 1¢ WWII defense stamp, postmarked Warwick, NY, AUG 1 1941. Dexter Press color lithograph of Greenwood Lake. Message: “Sure are having terrible weather. John is all crippled up in his back. Hope you folks are nearly settled at your place. Love, John & Irene.”

item.title: Card #163: Breckenridge, Missouri — High School Field Day (c. 1910)
item.description: From: Unknown | To: Mrs. R.H. Penney, Milan, Mo. | c. 1910. Palace Drug Co. Blue-tinted photo of Field Day at Breckenridge High School with hundreds of students assembled. Message: “Hello Folks: What are you doing? Preparing for winter? Come down for Thanksgiving and stay until Christmas.”

item.title: Card #162: Breckenridge, Missouri — Broadway Street (c. 1910)
item.description: From: Unknown | To: Mrs. Hector Cole, Milan, Mo. | Postmarked Breckenridge, MO, c. 1910. Palace Drug Co. Unpaved Broadway street scene. Message: “Hello, Was thinking of you, & thought would drop you a line. I am feeling fine & would like to have a lunch. I think of it so often & the time we had.”

item.title: Card #161: Unknown Location — Porch Portrait (March 7, 1908)
item.description: From: Rod (last name unknown) | To: Miss Verna Barnes, Salina, Kansas | Benjamin Franklin 1¢ stamp, postmarked March 7, 1908. Real photo postcard of five young people on a porch. Message: “Well we are back again working hard. The Floras are college girls (misses Campbell & Robertson). Ta-ta — Rod.”

item.title: Card #158: Toruń, Poland — The Nonnentor Gate (July 27, 1917)
item.description: From: Ulan P. Raatz, Reserve Squadron Uhlan Regiment 4, Thorn (WWI) | To: Fräulein Hilde Raaz, Salzwedel Altmark, Germany | Feldpost (German WWI military mail), postmarked THORN 27.7.17. Color lithograph of the medieval Nonnentor (Nuns' Gate) in Thorn (now Toruń, Poland). Birthday card from a soldier father to his daughter: "Dear little Hilde! On your birthday I send you the warmest wishes. May you spend the day in the best of health and much enjoyment. Kisses from your father." Front inscription adds greetings to Aunt Else, Uncle Paul, and little Hans.

media:thumbnail.url: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jeremy5ive/foundandsent/main/images/1927 - Torun, Poland - The Nonnentor Gate - front.jpeg

item.title: Card #159: Chicago, Illinois — Sheraton-Blackstone Hotel (November 25, 1957)
item.description: From: Unknown (Grandma or family member), Plainfield, Iowa | To: Douglas Fogland, 478A Route 1, Ft. Collins, CO | Liberty 3¢ stamp, postmarked Plainfield, Iowa, NOV 25 1957. Colourpicture Publishers, Boston. Vivid illustrated art of the Sheraton-Blackstone Hotel against the Chicago night skyline. A Christmas card sent to a child postcard collector: "Do you think that Santa will find you since you moved? Have the weather be real nice for Christmas so we can come & see you." Another Chicago hotel card in the archive.

item.title: Card #160: Shawnee State Park, Pennsylvania — Native Wild Bear (June 30, 1971)
item.description: From: Cricket & Doug, Shawnee State Park, PA | To: Miss Irene Morris, 16400 Cerfield Rd., Alliance, Ohio | Eisenhower 8¢ stamp, postmarked Bedford, PA, JUL 1 1971. Curt Teich Color card showing black bears on a fallen log in a pine forest. Message: "Hi there! I'm at Shawnee State Park near Schellsburg Pa. We got here Sunday evening about 5 o'clock. Haven't seen too many nice looking guys. Am having a real nice time. I'll write when I get back home. Love, Cricket & Doug."

item.title: Card #149: Caldwell County, Colorado — Mining Operation (January 15, 1907)
item.description: From: R.H. Bennett (Boise, Idaho) | To: Mr. R.V. Benney, Breckenridge, Missouri | Benjamin Franklin 1¢ green stamp, postmarked Boise, Idaho, Jan 15, 1907. Undivided back. Color lithograph of a Colorado mining complex. Message: "I am shipping you pre-paid a sack of Gold Ore. Look out for it!"

item.title: Card #150: Milan, Missouri — Baptist Church (July 12, 1912)
item.description: From: Bertha (last name unknown) | To: Unknown recipient, Milan, MO (address damaged) | Postmarked Milan, MO, JUL 12 PM 1912. Published by Mewmaw Bros., Milan, Mo. Message faded: "Give my regards to your father and mother. Love, Bertha."

item.title: Card #151: Ouray, Colorado — Camp Bird Road Overlook (October 4, 1973)
item.description: From: Unknown (signed "Jeyy"), Santa Barbara, CA | To: Erma Tuggle, 3315 Summit, Kansas City, MO 64111 | Written 10-4-73. Petley Studios, Phoenix, AZ. Cliff-edge jeep trail to Camp Bird Mine. Message: "Arrived in Santa Barbara Tues. morning after leaving Salt Lake City. Had a real nice visit with Pat & family. Will leave for home Mon. 10-8."

media:thumbnail.url: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jeremy5ive/foundandsent/main/images/1973 - Camp Bird Road Overlook - Quray, CO - front.jpeg

item.title: Card #152: Northern Indiana — Amish Farms, Wheat Harvest (1970)
item.description: From: Unknown (family member), Berrien Center, MI | To: Mrs. V.R. Stander, Anahuac, TX | Postmarked Berrien Center, Michigan, 1970. US Flag 6¢ stamp. Meter: "PRAY FOR PEACE." Penrod Studio / Dexter Press. Horse-drawn wheat harvest. Message: "We are eating so much I will probably gain 5 pounds. Everyone is just fine up here."

item.title: Card #153: New York, New York — St. Patrick's Cathedral (October 10, 1979)
item.description: From: Mom, New Haven, CT | To: Mr. & Mrs. Mitchell Kelley, Austin, TX 78723 | Written 10-10-79. USA 15¢ Seeing Eye Dog stamp. C. Harrison Conroy Co. Gothic twin spires against midtown Manhattan. Message: "Having a wonderful time. Went to NY on Amtrack. Snowed on us nearly all day. Went in this beautiful Cathedral today. Miss you. Love, Mom."

media:thumbnail.url: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jeremy5ive/foundandsent/main/images/1979 - St Patricks Cathedral - New York, NY - front.jpeg

item.title: Card #154: Reno, Nevada — The Biggest Little City at Night (August 9, 1990)
item.description: From: Mary Jane, Reno, NV | To: Mrs. Ruth Grady, St. Charles, MO | Postmarked AUG 9 1990, Postmark Jackpot Convention Station. Photo by Marino, Italcards, Italy. Iconic Reno arch at night. Message: "Enjoying the cheap prices of food, the free nickels twice a day, a bus ride to Virginia City. There's a beauty even in all the desert & nothingness. Love, Mary Jane."

item.title: Card #155: Miami, Florida — Skyline at Night (c. 1968)
item.description: From: Miss Agnes E. Weiland, Miami, FL | To: Mr. & Mrs. Emil Jensen, 3309 Collingwood, Detroit, MI | Thomas Jefferson 2¢ stamp, c. 1968. Lusterchrome card by Tichnor Bros., Boston. Night skyline of Miami reflected in Biscayne Bay. Message: "Dear Friends: Thanks for the literature. We can always learn something more about God's Word & his promises to us. We pray for his Kingdom to come on Earth. Sincerely for Truth, Miss Agnes E. Weiland."
